payload.claim:
Any one of the following would change the view:
- Upgrade case: FCF turns sustainably positive as the Karlskrona expansion completes, while gross margin holds above 33% and annual share dilution stops. Together these would turn scarcity returns into owner earnings and widen the margin of safety.
- Downgrade case, margins: TTM gross margin falls back below 32%.
- Downgrade case, pricing and execution: a material project loss or cable-fault provision, or evidence of HV pricing pressure in new awards (falling backlog margins, competitors' capacity coming online, offshore wind auction cancellations).
- Downgrade case, integrity: any escalation of the integrity gate beyond Flag.

prediction.reasoning: TTM gross margin has stepped up from 33.16% to 33.96% to 34.42% as scarcity-priced HV backlog is executed. That should keep the rolling margin above 33.5% for at least two more quarters, before any capacity-cycle normalisation shows up. My disagreement with the price lies further out, on whether these margins persist for a decade, not on whether they hold in the next two quarters.
